questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The courses that the university of Oslo offered and is specialized in. The courses, maritime law and transport law, have not been offered the last few years on Copenhagen University. Besides from the academic opportunities and possible carrier opportunities in the future, the personal connection to Norway as a neighbor country to Denmark was also one of the main reason to studying in Oslo. I have always been interested in the history that Denmark and Norway shares. The connection between the Norwegian and Danish culture. Especially the Norwegian language. I wanted to improve my Norwegian language, but alsio to understand the development of the Norwegian language better. In many ways, I think that the Danish language could learn a lot from Norwegian Bokmål. In addition to the choosing the destination, exploring the nature in Norway was also one of the main reason to choose Oslo Universitet. The mountains, the fjords and the natural phenomenas that Norway can offer was definitely also a main factor for choosing Oslo. Furthermore, it is easily to explore the nature such as the mountains, the fjords in Oslo. It only takes 30-40 min. with the tramp to go to the mountains. You can in the Summer or in the Autumn visit the many islands that are in Oslo Fjords and in the Winther you can easily go skiing in the mountains. 

It is also easy to go and explore other cities in Norway such as Bergen, Stavanger, Trondheim with flight. 

However, Norway is not cheap, which is also worth to consider before going to Norway.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't regret studying abroad, however the University of Oslo does not provide the most structured and best lectures, which made the stay a bit stressfull as a student in a new country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find information, when it came to the University of Oslo. I was lucky that I understood a bit Norwegian and had a roomie, who also studied law, but I heard from other exchange students that they found it difficult to access informations easily.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The buddy week was a huge help. The buddies did their best to help, but of course they could not answer all the questions, which is understandable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own since I wanted to live with some Norwegian students, so I could improve my Norwegian.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The best advice I can give you is to share a flat with other people. I can recommend to live with other Norwegian people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a bit confused about the registration process. However, I received help from my own university and the buddies from the buddy week.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was not sure, if I got the courses that I have registrated. Especially because my Learning Agreement was first signed after I started at the University.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had to contact the exchange coordinator. However, she replied quickly afterwards.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was successful. I got all the courses that I wanted, so I was pleased to get them, even though the registration process was a bit stressfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Send the exchange coordinator a message at our own university as well as the hos university, if you are in doubt. And if you don't get an answer in a reasonable amount of time then write to them again.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no structure or access to information. Many of the lectures was cancelled in last minute, and there was not always a reading list publiced before the lecture. You could therefore not be prepared for the lecture, which of course had an affect on the lecture and what you gain from it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was higher than compared at m own university. Probably because the syllable was in English, so it was more difficult and took longer time to prepare for the lectures in the beginning. However, the expectations and the reading list in one of the courses was to high considered that the courses was in English. The same was the expectations for the exam. Even Norwegian students found the level too high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The University of Oslo only teach with lectures. There are no seminars. It was not a problem in the courses of maritime law, since we only were around 30 students and with zoom only sometimes 5-10 students, who met physical to the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Maritime Law: Contract 
Maritime Law: Liability and Insurance
International Environmental Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Maritime Law: Contract 
Maritime Law: Liability and Insurance 

Most of the lectures are held by lawyers, who are leading in the area that the teach in. The level is high and you can learn a lot from them. Besides from that the courses are not offered at the University of Copenhagen.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I encountered extra for food and living costs. I did not want to say no to go to a concert with my friends even if it was a bit expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I did expect that meat would be expensive in Norway, but the milk, butter and cheese are also expensive compared to Danish prices. 

I thought that vegetables would be expensive, it was less expensive than considered. Norwegian chocolate was also less expensive than compared to Danish chocolate.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had fitness membership. It was less expensive than it would have been in Denmark with many good facilities such as biking, yoga, pilates, but also cold bath and sauna. 

There was also a lot of clubs, however I did not participate as much in the end of the stay.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You could sign up for the a membership at Athletica, which had fitness center over the most of the city. 

The faculty of law also offered many social activities such as Amnesty International, a student pub, a choir and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: We were a small group, who did isbathing every Sunday in Sørenga. I can definitely recommend that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: First and foremost I would recommend other students to relax and enjoy the city. Use the weekend to go in Oslo City. Dont hesitate to go to visit a lot of other places in Norway. Explore Oslo City and find you favorite café.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust to the Norwegian culture as it more or less reminds a lot about the Danish. However for me it was more the difficulties between Norwegian and Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go one Friday with your friends to the student pub.  You have to take initiative to learn the local students to know. They can seem as they are not interested in get to know you, but you just have to give it a try. It is not you that there is something wrong with, it is just how the socializing culture in Norway is. But most of the time the Norwegian students are really helpful and kind.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Norwegian people are very polite and they really want to help you, if you ask for help, so instead of thinking that that you are asking to much just accept their help and say thank you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate that the Norwegian people are polite, helpful and open-minded.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you have a question or are in doubt ask for help UCPH replies fast, if you don't receive an answer from the exchange coordinator. 

Ask the professor, if he/she contacts you on Webmail or Studentweb about the syllables and cancelled lectures, but also about how the exam is held. 

See if you can buy your books used.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Meet up personal and ask the studentinformation on first floor. They are very helpfull.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get new friends from other parts of the World, but also to get Norwegian friends and an affiliation to Norway.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To balance between studying and personal developing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
